options.text: Sedimentation lets heavier sand settle, and decantation pours off the liquid above it.
The settling of sand at the bottom is itself called decantation.
The same settling-and-pour method will separate dissolved sugar from sugar water.
After pouring, no tiny sand grain can remain in the liquid that was poured off.

stem:
Tanya leaves a mixture of water and playground sand undisturbed in a tall jar. After the sand settles, she carefully pours off the clearer water.

Which statement is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Sedimentation settles heavier insoluble sand; decantation pours off the liquid above it. Dissolved sugar does not settle; some fine grains can remain suspended.
